content.text:
Focused tests, typechecking, and the MCP bundle build pass, but valid runtime templates can lose Tailwind styling and duplicate pie labels can receive incorrect per-item colors.

Full review comments:

- [P2] Safelist classes supplied by stored templates — /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/mcp-app-prod-fetch/packages/owletto/vite.config.mcp.ts:50-56
  When a stored `payload_template` supplies `props.className`, those runtime strings cannot be discovered from these build-time source files. Replacing the shared Tailwind import with `source(none)` therefore removes previously available utilities such as `space-y-3`, `gap-4`, and arbitrary grid classes while `McpJsonTemplateView` still emits those class names, causing valid stored cards to silently lose layout styling. Include a fixed DSL utility safelist/source before disabling the broad scan.

- [P2] Keep pie styles aligned with their source rows — /Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/.claude/worktrees/mcp-app-prod-fetch/packages/owletto/src/mcp-apps/interaction/json-template-view.tsx:409-414
  When pie data contains repeated `nameField` values with distinct per-slice `itemStyle` colors, `find` returns the first matching row for every duplicate, so later slices receive the wrong color. Pie labels are not required to be unique; retain each source index through normalization/filtering instead of looking the row up by label.
